mil5.2.6:1.2: ‘One who takes life without knowing it generates greater demerit.’
mil5.2.6:1.3: Yet the Blessed One also said in the Vinaya regulations:
mil5.2.6:1.4: ‘There is no offence for one who does not know.’
mil5.2.6:1.5: If, Venerable Nāgasena, one who takes life unknowingly generates greater demerit, then the statement ‘There is no offence for one who does not know’ is false.
mil5.2.6:1.6: And if there is no offence for one who does not know, then the statement ‘One who takes life unknowingly generates greater demerit’ is also false.
mil5.2.6:1.7: This too is a two-horned dilemma, hard to cross and hard to get past, that has come to you; you must resolve it.”
mil5.2.6:2.1: “This too was said by the Blessed One, your majesty, ‘One who takes life without knowing it generates greater demerit.’
mil5.2.6:2.2: But it was also said by the Blessed One in the Vinaya:
mil5.2.6:2.3: ‘There is no offence for one who does not know.’
mil5.2.6:2.4: But there is a difference in meaning between the two.
mil5.2.6:2.6: There is, your majesty, an offence that is released by perception, and there is an offence that is not released by perception.
mil5.2.6:2.7: It is with reference to the offence that is released by perception, your majesty, that the Blessed One said:
mil5.2.6:2.8: ‘There is no offence for one who does not know.’”
mil5.2.6:2.9: “Well said, Venerable Nāgasena. It is so, and I accept it.”
